findings.claim: The plan does not say what an index entry is, but three other tickets write entries for this check to read: new-doc-verb adds to docs/README.md 'in the format kmctl check reads', new-concept-verbs adds to section indexes, and scaffold-init writes the empty docs/README.md. If the plan does not fix the contract (for example: a relative markdown link in the index whose target is a page in that folder or below; external links, anchors and links back out of the folder are not entries), the builder picks one and the writers may not match it, and kmctl check then fails on files kmctl wrote itself.

'It does not repeat what the okf validator checks' contradicts the done criterion for .okf/. okf_validate.py 0.10.1 in --strict already fails on a cross-link whose target is missing, which includes an index entry with no file. Read literally, the clause drops the 'entry with no file' check for .okf/. But kmctl never runs the validator: it is a test-only copy, and ci-action runs only kmctl check, so dropping the check leaves CI blind to it. The plan should say what the clause excludes (front matter, reserved names) and that kmctl check covers both directions for docs/ and .okf/. It should also say how this differs from link-check, which checks the same relative links later.

Scope leaves out the root index count. .claude/rules/okf-bundle.md (okf-indexes-track-their-directory and every-touched-concept-is-logged) requires the root index's counts to match, new-concept-verbs updates that count, and nothing else in kmctl checks it. Today the count is free prose ('9 concepts: the manifesto and 1 section.'), so checking it means pinning a parseable format that scaffold-init and new-concept-verbs also write. The plan should either take it in and say the format, or say it is out of scope and why.

Index entry format undefined. Resolved: the plan defines which index, what an entry is (list item, first relative link to a page in that folder or below, prototype README.md), and the three writer plans cite it.

'Does not repeat the validator' conflicted with checking .okf/ entries. Resolved: kmctl checks .okf/ entries itself because it does not run the validator; only front matter and spec conformance are left to the validator.
Root index count unaddressed. Resolved: kmctl neither writes nor checks counts; the repo's okf-bundle rule still mentions counts and adapt-copied-rules rewrites it.

_entries treats list items inside fenced code blocks as index entries, so an index that shows an example entry in a code fence fails with "entry links example.md, which does not exist". A list item in a fence is not a markdown list item, so this breaks the plan's entry definition and gives a false failure.

The plan says an entry links a page "in that folder or below", but _entries accepts any relative target, including ../outside.md, and _check_index then reports it as a missing entry file when it does not exist. That is link-check's job, not the index check's. Non-blocking because the fix is plain (drop targets that resolve outside index.parent) and needs one test.

Hidden folders are handled two ways. check_okf skips dot-folders as sections, but docs/ rglob and _section_concepts rglob still pick up .md files under dot-folders (docs/.hidden/x.md is reported as unlisted, so a docs/.vitepress/ tree would fail). Pick one rule and apply it everywhere. Non-blocking because the fix is a filter plus a test.

index.read_text() uses the locale encoding and raises on a non-UTF-8 index, so kmctl check crashes with a UnicodeDecodeError traceback. cli-interface.md requires a one-line stderr refusal and a nonzero exit, or the bad file could be reported as a finding. Use encoding="utf-8" and handle the decode error. Non-blocking because the fix is local.

Gaps against the docstring and type-hint rules. _rel and _section_concepts have no docstrings. Finding has no numpy Attributes section, and level is a plain str where it could be Literal["error", "skipped"]. The test helpers _write, _good_repo, _check and _findings have no docstrings, and _check has no return annotation.

cli-interface.md help-is-tested asks for tests that each verb's help names what it produces, gives every input an example, and renders at 80 columns. No help test covers the new check verb, and none exists for any verb yet (pre-existing, but the rules say to fix it when found). Non-blocking because adding the test does not change behaviour.

entries.change: Entries inside code fences and links that leave the index's folder are ignored, hidden files are not pages, a non-UTF-8 index is a finding instead of a crash, and helpers and Finding have docstrings and a Literal level.
Tests for fenced example entries, links leaving the folder, hidden pages and a non-UTF-8 index; test helpers get docstrings and a return type.
New help test for every verb, so init and check both have one; help fits 80 columns, names what it produces, and each non-flag input has a metavar and an Examples epilog.
